title: Align Read tool with the TS baseline
objective: Implement all Read improvements identified by the per-tool subagent report so the Go clone matches the original TypeScript tool in public contract, runtime logic, robustness, state lifecycle, and tests.

context.problem: Go Read covers the core happy paths for text, range reads, notebooks, images, PDF attachments, ReadState, and several rich-result metadata probes, but it is not fully TS-exact. The highest-risk gaps are runtime and lifecycle differences: Go dedups reads from broader state than TS and stamps rich reads into state, PDF page selection/model/extraction behavior is a Go-only superset, cyber-risk reminder gating is not wired to the active model and can affect rich outputs, skill discovery and analytics/listeners fire at different times with different payloads, and the Go tool boundary lacks TS strict/output/permission metadata. Focused verification was run with `go test ./tools -run 'Test(FileReadTool|ReadFileState|CyberReminderGating|Alignment_FileRead)' -count=1` and currently fails at `TestFileReadToolRejectsOpenEndedPDFRangesOverLimit`, confirming one PDF selector parity gap.

parallelization_notes: Can be assigned to an implementation subagent after listed dependencies are available. Avoid running concurrently with another task that owns the same files.

improvement_points.title: Read does not expose the TS output/tool contract as a first-class Go contract
improvement_points.description: TS Read is a strict tool with an outputSchema discriminated by `type` (`text`, `image`, `notebook`, `pdf`, `parts`, `file_unchanged`) and tool metadata for max result size, read-only, concurrency, search/read classification, and auto-classifier input. Go has the public tool name and increasingly rich `ContentBlocks`/Metadata, but the shared tool interface is still Execute-only, the JSON schema cannot express strict-object rejection, and the TS result union is not the primary result contract. This leaves downstream consumers relying on string content plus metadata rather than the same structured shape TS returns.

improvement_points.title: file_unchanged dedup applies to broader state and richer formats than TS
improvement_points.description: TS dedups only prior full Read-origin text/notebook state: it requires a non-partial entry whose `offset` is defined, and image/PDF branches never populate readFileState. Edit/Write/NotebookEdit deliberately write `offset: undefined` so the next Read cannot dedup against post-write state. Go checks only offset, limit, and mtime, ignores LastTool/source, stamps rich image/notebook/PDF reads into state, and uses a different file_unchanged stub. This can suppress content in Go where TS would re-read and can point the model at stale or unavailable prior rich content.

improvement_points.title: Cyber-risk reminder gating is not wired like TS and can be appended to rich results
improvement_points.description: TS appends the cyber-risk reminder only in the text result mapper and uses the active main-loop model to skip exempt models. Go has a compatible constant and model exemption helper, but the active model is only set through a test/config setter and is not wired in SetupRegistry. When unset, Go falls back to path/content heuristics, so benign project files on non-exempt models may omit the TS reminder. Go also calls the append helper after rich reads, modifying ContentBlocks and Content for image/PDF/notebook summaries where TS does not append the reminder.

improvement_points.title: PDF page selection, model support, page-count fallback, and extraction lifecycle diverge
improvement_points.description: TS accepts a single page, bounded range, or open-ended range string syntactically, then rejects any open-ended range at validation time because it treats Infinity as over the 20-page cap. Go accepts comma-separated selectors, deduplicates pages, resolves open-ended selectors against real page count, and has tests for comma lists. TS page counting uses only `pdfinfo` and returns null on failure; Go falls back to Swift and raw byte scanning. TS rejects full PDF reads on unsupported Haiku 3 models and persists extracted page images under the tool results directory with an `outputDir` in the `parts` result. Go has no visible model support gate, uses temp extraction directories removed before returning, and returns only supplemental image NewMessages for pages.

improvement_points.title: Read path permission/observer lifecycle is approximated inside Execute
improvement_points.description: TS Read participates in the central permission and observable-input lifecycle before the tool call: it expands observable paths, exposes getPath, prepares wildcard permission matchers, checks explicit read-deny rules without I/O, and bypasses UNC I/O before permission. Go enforces allowed directories and verifies the opened file descriptor, which is strong local safety, but the shared Tool interface has no Read-specific permission hooks or observable-input backfill. Generic parsing also ignores unknown keys, so TS strict-object rejection is not enforced at runtime.

improvement_points.title: File reading limits and token counting do not follow TS precedence or exact counter path
improvement_points.description: TS computes default file-reading limits from env var, GrowthBook override, and hardcoded defaults, then lets ToolUseContext override maxSizeBytes/maxTokens and logs override analytics. Token validation estimates first and then calls the API tokenizer near the limit. Go uses constants for text size/token limits, has an optional TokenBudgetProvider only for rich image/PDF budgets, and SetupRegistry does not wire that provider. Text token checks use a Go tiktoken estimate path rather than TS API counting, so boundary behavior and operational controls can differ.

improvement_points.title: Skill discovery timing and conditional activation do not match TS session lifecycle
improvement_points.description: TS discovers nearby skill directories and activates conditional skills after dedup but before the file read, skips the whole flow in CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE, records dynamicSkillDirTriggers for attachment display, and starts directory loading asynchronously. Go invokes discovery only after a successful read, has no visible simple-mode guard in FileReadTool, ignores per-name trigger matches, and the skills Manager conditional activation hook is effectively a cache-warming no-op. This changes which reads can surface skills and when they become active or visible.

improvement_points.title: Read analytics and listener scope/signatures differ from TS
improvement_points.description: TS fileReadListeners receive `(filePath, content)` and are called only on the text read path after the content is available. TS session analytics includes total/read lines, total/read bytes, offset, optional limit, extension, optional messageID, and session-memory/session-transcript booleans. Go invokes basic and rich listeners for every successful read variant with mtime/partial/byte/line metadata but no content, emits a simplified `tengu_session_file_read`, and emits a second kind-based event for session files. The gap is not just field names; it changes listener side effects and analytics cardinality.

improvement_points.title: Path expansion and per-session cwd normalization are not TS-equivalent for base Read
improvement_points.description: TS expandPath trims input, expands `~`, resolves relative paths against async-local getCwd, converts Windows POSIX-style paths, and normalizes NFC before validation, permission checks, and state keys. Go base Read trims file_path and uses filepath.Abs/Clean around the process cwd and ReadState key normalization. Agent-specific wrappers rewrite relative paths for subagents, but base FileReadTool is not injected with RuntimeScope/current cwd, so session cwd, home expansion, NFC, and Windows path conversion semantics are not the same at the core tool boundary.

improvement_points.title: Read parity tests include stale comments, Go-only expectations, and one currently failing selector test
improvement_points.description: The Go test suite has useful coverage but does not yet form a clean TS parity baseline. Some alignment-test comments still say every case should fail even though the implementation now has FileReadResult and variant metadata. Other tests explicitly lock Go-only behavior such as comma-separated PDF page selectors. A focused Read test command currently fails on open-ended PDF range handling, which is a real parity mismatch against TS validation.

implementation_subtasks.title: Expose a TS-equivalent Read output/tool contract
implementation_steps: Decide the Go carrier for TS Read data: either a typed Read result embedded in ToolResult metadata/structured content or a shared output-schema mechanism used by all tools.
Make Read expose all TS variants with their required per-variant fields, including file_unchanged and parts/outputDir if PDF extraction parity is implemented in READ-TASK-004.
Add strict schema support or a Read-specific strict parser that rejects unknown keys.
Expose/read through metadata for maxResultSizeChars=Infinity, strict=true, read-only, concurrency-safe, search/read classification, and auto-classifier input.
acceptance_criteria: Read has a model/runtime-visible structured contract equivalent to TS `text|image|notebook|pdf|parts|file_unchanged`.
Unknown Read input keys are rejected or otherwise cannot reach Execute silently.
Read is discoverable as read-only and concurrency-safe, with maxResultSizeChars=Infinity or an equivalent no-persist policy.
Existing text/image/notebook/PDF happy-path behavior remains available through the model-visible result.
risks: Changing the shared ToolResult contract can affect every tool; keep Read-specific bridges isolated unless a shared contract migration is explicitly planned.
non_goals: Do not redesign unrelated tool result schemas in the same task.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align ReadState dedup origin, rich-format state, and file_unchanged stub
implementation_steps: Mark Read-origin state explicitly, or make dedup require an entry shape that only Read text/notebook writes can produce.
Stop rich image/PDF reads from populating dedup-eligible ReadState entries unless TS adds the same behavior.
Ensure Edit/Write/NotebookEdit refreshed entries can satisfy stale-write checks but cannot satisfy Read dedup.
Replace Go file_unchanged model text with the exact TS FILE_UNCHANGED_STUB.
Consider a feature flag/killswitch equivalent if the runtime needs to disable dedup like TS GrowthBook can.
acceptance_criteria: Second identical full text or notebook Read returns file_unchanged only when prior eligible Read content is still in context and mtime/range match.
Reads after Write/Edit/NotebookEdit never dedup against the post-write state entry.
Image and PDF reads do not produce file_unchanged on repeat under default TS-parity behavior.
Partial reads do not dedup as full reads.
The file_unchanged model-visible text exactly matches TS.
risks: FileEdit/FileWrite depend on the same state store for stale-write checks; do not remove state fields needed by write/edit guards.
non_goals: Do not change NotebookEdit stale-read semantics beyond what is needed to keep post-edit Read dedup from firing.

implementation_subtasks.title: Wire cyber-risk reminder to active model and restrict it to text reads
implementation_steps: Plumb the active main-loop model into Read cyber gating during registry/provider setup.
Remove the default path/content heuristic from TS-parity execution, or gate it behind a documented non-TS compatibility mode.
Call reminder append only from the text result path.
Keep the exempt model list aligned with TS canonical model names.
acceptance_criteria: For every non-exempt active model, text Read appends the TS reminder regardless of path/content.
For exempt models, text Read omits the reminder even for suspicious paths/content.
Image, PDF, parts, notebook, and file_unchanged results do not receive an extra reminder block under default TS-parity behavior.
Tests cover model unset, non-exempt, exempt, suspicious content, and rich read variants.
risks: Provider/model state may be mutable at runtime; avoid a one-time stale model capture if the provider can swap models mid-session.
non_goals: Do not alter the reminder text unless the TS constant changes.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align PDF selector grammar, model gate, page counting, and extraction artifact lifecycle
dependencies: READ-TASK-001 if `parts` outputDir must be represented as typed Read output.
implementation_steps: Change default PDF page parser to TS grammar: single page, bounded range, and open-ended range only; remove comma lists from TS-parity mode.
Reject open-ended ranges during pre-I/O validation the way TS does, because Infinity exceeds the 20-page cap.
Make page count behavior match TS pdfinfo-only semantics unless a documented compatibility mode is explicitly enabled.
Add an isPDFSupported-equivalent active-model gate for full PDF reads.
Persist extracted page images under the Go equivalent of tool results and return a typed `parts` result with outputDir, then build supplemental image messages from that directory.
acceptance_criteria: `pages: "1,3"` and other comma selectors are rejected by default with the TS invalid-pages message.
`pages: "3-"` is rejected before file I/O with the TS max-pages message.
Full PDF reads on unsupported models return the TS unsupported-model message and do not inline a document block.
When extraction succeeds, the result includes count/originalSize/outputDir and the page images remain available for consumers for the expected lifecycle.
Large PDF, small PDF, explicit pages, missing poppler, empty/corrupt/password-protected PDFs are covered by tests.
risks: Removing comma-list support may break Go users relying on the extension; hide it behind an opt-in if compatibility is required.
non_goals: Do not implement text extraction from PDFs; TS Read sends document/page image content, not extracted text.

implementation_subtasks.title: Bridge Read into TS-style permission, observable path, and strict validation lifecycle
implementation_steps: Add optional tool metadata/hooks for getPath, observable input backfill, permission matcher, and read permission checks, or implement a focused Read adapter consumed by the runtime.
Make Read parse strict input and reject unknown keys before I/O.
Preserve current fd verification while adding a no-I/O deny/UNC path stage before opening/statting.
Route permission-denied and invalid-input errors through TS-equivalent message/error semantics where the Go runtime supports them.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown Read input keys are rejected before filesystem access.
Observable/tool-use consumers see expanded Read file_path values equivalent to TS.
Explicit denied read paths are rejected before I/O.
UNC-style paths are not probed before the permission lifecycle can decide.
AllowedDirs/fd verification still protects symlink and TOCTOU escapes.
risks: Permission lifecycle changes are cross-cutting; keep the first task limited to Read hooks and strict parsing unless a shared framework migration is already approved.
non_goals: Do not weaken existing fd verification to match TS; it is compatible as an additional post-permission safety check.

implementation_subtasks.title: Implement TS file-reading limits, context overrides, and token-count behavior
implementation_steps: Introduce a FileReadingLimits provider with TS precedence: env override, experiment/config override, defaults, and per-call/session context override.
Wire limits into FileReadTool from SetupRegistry/runtime context.
Log the override analytics event when per-context overrides are supplied.
Decide and implement a TS-equivalent precise token counter path, or isolate current local estimation behind a documented non-TS fallback.
acceptance_criteria: CLAUDE_CODE_FILE_READ_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS controls text read token limits like TS.
Runtime context can override maxTokens and maxSizeBytes per Read call/session.
Read prompt guidance can reflect includeMaxSizeInPrompt and targetedRangeNudge flags if those prompts are surfaced in Go.
Token-limit boundary tests match TS fixtures for below, near, and above maxTokens.
Override analytics is emitted only when an override is present.
risks: An API-backed token counter may require provider access; if unavailable, tests should clearly mark the remaining difference rather than silently treating estimates as parity.
non_goals: Do not change image compression/token budgeting except where it depends on the same active token budget provider.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align Read-driven skill discovery and conditional activation lifecycle
implementation_steps: Move Read skill discovery to the TS timing point: after dedup miss and before the inner read work.
Add a CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE guard to skip Read-driven discovery/activation.
Represent dynamicSkillDirTriggers or the Go equivalent so attachment/listing consumers can see why directories were surfaced.
Implement per-name conditional activation rather than discarding LookupDynamicSkillsForPath results.
Keep directory loading best-effort/non-blocking if the Go runtime supports asynchronous loading safely.
acceptance_criteria: A read near a skill directory surfaces/activates the skill before content handling completes, matching TS lifecycle expectations.
Dedup hits do not run the discovery path if TS does not run it for that branch.
CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE disables Read-driven skill discovery.

non_goals: Do not rewrite the whole Skill tool; focus on Read-triggered discovery and activation.

dependencies: READ-TASK-002 if listener/dedup behavior depends on eligible state entries.
implementation_steps: Add a TS-compatible listener path that receives resolved file path and textual content for text reads only.
Keep any Go rich listener as an explicitly separate non-TS extension if still needed.

implementation_subtasks.title: Normalize Read paths and cwd handling to TS expandPath semantics
dependencies: READ-TASK-005 if observable-input backfill and permission hooks are implemented first.
implementation_steps: Introduce a Go expandReadPath helper matching TS trim, empty path, ~, relative cwd, Windows POSIX conversion where applicable, and Unicode normalization behavior.
Inject RuntimeScope/current cwd into FileReadTool so base session Read does not depend on process cwd.
Use the expanded path consistently for permission checks, fd verification, state keys, analytics, and displayed file paths where TS does.
Keep agent cwd wrapping compatible or remove duplicated rewriting once FileReadTool itself is scoped.
acceptance_criteria: `~`, `~/x`, whitespace-padded paths, relative paths, and empty/whitespace paths resolve like TS.

macOS screenshot thin-space fallback still works after the broader expansion change.
